clue.text: Fans of a departing horse making animal noises

parts.note: the letter A is the one that departs

indicators.note: something departing leaves, so the named letter goes out of the word for the young horse

parts.note: a foal is a young horse; losing its A leaves FOL
lowing is the sound cattle make

explanation.surface: Racing fans make farmyard sounds as a horse leaves the paddock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Fans' looks like the subject of the sentence, but it is the definition, read as a noun for supporters.
explanation.definitionFit: A following is a body of supporters, so it is a collective noun for fans.

clue.text: Strength of warning about Tesla

indicators.note: about means going around, so the golfer's cry wraps round the unit

parts.note: the warning shout on a golf course
T is the symbol for the tesla, the unit of magnetic flux density

explanation.surface: A question about how strong a warning about an electric car maker needs to be.
explanation.walkthrough: Tesla looks like the car company, but it is the SI unit, symbol T.
explanation.definitionFit: A forte is one's strong point, a particular talent or skill.

clue.text: Young runner always allowed outside

indicators.note: the word for permitted is placed on the outside, enclosing the other word

parts.note: let means permitted
ever means always, as in for ever

explanation.surface: A young athlete has always been permitted to go outdoors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Young runner' suggests a junior athlete; it is a baby hare, a famously fast runner.
explanation.definitionFit: A leveret is a hare in its first year, and hares are swift running animals.

clue.text: Paddled in sea after boat discovered

indicators.note: dis-covered means the covering outer letters are stripped, leaving only the inside

parts.note: the inner letters once the outer pair is removed
the Red Sea, so a sea can be RED

explanation.surface: Someone rowed in the sea once a boat was found.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after' puts the sea's name after the uncovered boat; discovered means uncovered, not found.
explanation.definitionFit: Oared means propelled with oars, which is to say paddled or rowed.

clue.text: Set up home above stable?

parts.note: being in means being at home
a stall is a compartment for an animal in a stable, hence the question mark

explanation.surface: Building a house over the stables.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'above' means the first piece sits on top of the second; the question mark flags that a stall is only part of a stable.
explanation.definitionFit: To install something is to put it in place and set it up ready for use.

clue.text: Applicable to any group that's playing Carnegie Hall at last

indicators.note: playing suggests the letters perform in a fresh order

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word it follows

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: Any band that plays Carnegie Hall, the New York concert venue, at last.
explanation.definitionFit: Generical is an old form of generic, describing something that covers a whole class or group.

clue.text: Yawn, as fruit recipe lost

indicators.note: something lost is gone, so that letter is taken away

parts.note: a grape is a fruit
R is the abbreviation for recipe, from Latin, as on prescriptions

explanation.surface: Someone yawns with boredom after losing the recipe for a fruit dish.
explanation.definitionFit: To gape is to open the mouth wide, which is what a yawn does.

clue.text: When is boring right-wing politician getting new cooker?

indicators.note: boring means drilling into, so this word goes inside the politician's name

parts.note: Michael Gove, a Conservative cabinet minister
as means when, as in 'as I left'
N is the abbreviation for new

explanation.surface: A jibe asking when a dull Tory MP will buy a new cooker.
explanation.walkthrough: 'boring' looks like an insult to the politician, but it means drilling into, an instruction to put one piece inside another.
explanation.definitionFit: A gas oven is a kind of cooker fuelled by gas.

clue.text: Divided and cut up stem on daffodil, primarily

indicators.note: in a down clue up means reading from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: to lop is to cut off; read upwards it gives POL
to stem from is to arise from

indicators.note: primarily points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the first letter of the flower

explanation.surface: A gardener divides a daffodil bulb and cuts its stem.
explanation.walkthrough: 'stem' looks like part of the daffodil but is the verb meaning arise.
explanation.definitionFit: Polarised describes opinion split into two opposing camps, so it means divided.

clue.text: Issues about extremely short book

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the issues wrap around the other word

parts.note: probs is informal for problems, i.e. issues

indicators.note: short means cut off before the end, so the final letter is dropped

parts.note: very means extremely; cut short it is VER

explanation.surface: Complaints about a book being far too short.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Issues' looks like editions of a publication, but it is informal for problems.
explanation.definitionFit: Proverbs is a book of the Old Testament, a collection of wise sayings.

clue.text: Cherish women about to be thrown out of city

indicators.note: thrown out of means expelled, so these letters are removed from the city's name

parts.note: the city in north-east England
W is the abbreviation for women
CA is circa, about

explanation.surface: A cherished group of women about to be expelled from a city.
explanation.walkthrough: Removing W and CA from NEWCASTLE leaves NESTLE.
explanation.definitionFit: To nestle someone is to hold them close and snug, an affectionate sense of cherish.

clue.text: Four astute tradesmen's stocks

indicators.note: a shop stocks goods, so the phrase holds the answer within it

parts.note: spans the end of the first word and start of the second

explanation.surface: Four shrewd shopkeepers and what they sell.
explanation.definitionFit: A tetrad is a group or set of four things.

clue.text: Varadkar shot burrowing mammal

indicators.note: something shot is wrecked or broken, so the name's letters are rearranged

parts.note: Leo Varadkar, former Irish Taoiseach

explanation.surface: An Irish politician shoots an animal that digs burrows.
explanation.definitionFit: The aardvark is an African mammal that digs burrows and feeds on ants and termites.

clue.text: Walk unsteadily in summer?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: to stagger or wobble
second meaning: one who adds up figures, from tot up

explanation.surface: Wondering whether hot weather makes people stagger.
explanation.walkthrough: 'summer' is not the season but someone who sums; to tot up is to add.
explanation.definitionFit: A totter staggers, and is also, by playful coinage, a person who tots up a sum.

clue.text: Sniper who lost control

indicators.note: something lost has gone astray, so these letters wander into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A marksman who lost his self-control.
explanation.definitionFit: Ownership means possession and control of something.

clue.text: Vin rouge? It's not for consumption when driving on public roads

definitions.text: It's not for consumption when driving on public roads

parts.note: rouge is French for red
Vin Diesel, the American actor, so Vin stands for his surname

explanation.surface: Red wine, and a warning that it should not be drunk while driving.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Vin rouge' reads as French red wine, but Vin is the actor's first name, so it becomes red Diesel. Red diesel is cheaper, dyed fuel for farm and off-road vehicles.
explanation.definitionFit: Red diesel is lower-taxed fuel that is illegal to use in vehicles on public roads.

clue.text: Claims no drunk can display brevity

indicators.note: a drunk stumbles about, so these letters lurch into a new order

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone insists a drunk can still keep things short.
explanation.definitionFit: Laconism is terseness of speech, using few words, which is brevity.

clue.text: Geraint and Emily secretly together

indicators.note: something held secretly is concealed, here inside the run of names

parts.note: runs across the end of the first name, the middle word and the start of the second name

explanation.surface: Two people, Geraint and Emily, are secretly a couple.
explanation.definitionFit: In tandem means working jointly, side by side, as a pair.

clue.text: Scared, in dangerous situation for 1920s Chicago Feds

definitions.meaning: second meaning, read as two words: the gangster Al Capone carrying a weapon

explanation.surface: Federal agents in Prohibition-era Chicago feel frightened in a tight spot.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as AL ARMED: Al Capone with a gun was a peril to the federal agents chasing him.
explanation.definitionFit: Alarmed means frightened or anxious about a danger.

clue.text: Employee on public transport repeated phrase in meditation

parts.note: to man is to staff, and a man is a worker
a tram is a form of public transport

explanation.surface: A worker on a tram murmurs the same words to himself.
explanation.definitionFit: A mantram, a variant of mantra, is a word or phrase chanted over and over during meditation.

clue.text: Superior passport perhaps found in Russian vehicle

indicators.note: found in means located inside, so one piece sits within the other

parts.note: Lada is a Russian car brand
a passport is an example of identification, ID

explanation.surface: A posh passport turns up inside a Russian car.
explanation.definitionFit: La-di-da describes someone affectedly genteel or snobbish, putting on superior airs.

clue.text: Take out of the freezer food initially stored badly

indicators.note: badly suggests the letters are put together wrongly, in a new order
initially points to the first letter of the word before it

parts.note: the opening letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: Food kept poorly in the freezer has to be taken out.
explanation.definitionFit: To defrost frozen food is to thaw it after removing it from cold storage.

clue.text: Development of chemical process involving carbon migration

indicators.note: migration means moving to a new place, so carbon's letter moves and the word is rearranged

parts.note: a chemical reaction

explanation.surface: A chemistry write-up on a process where carbon moves around.
explanation.walkthrough: Only the C moves: shift it from fourth place to the front of REACTION. C is the symbol for carbon.
explanation.definitionFit: Creation is the act of bringing something into being, its development.

clue.text: Polish film in trouble

parts.note: to buff is to polish
E.T., the Spielberg film

explanation.surface: A movie from Poland runs into difficulties.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Polish' with its capital looks like the nationality; it is the verb to shine.
explanation.definitionFit: To buffet is to batter repeatedly, as wind or misfortune troubles someone.

clue.text: Rod is bachelor, and not stuck up

parts.note: BA, Bachelor of Arts

indicators.note: in a down clue up means read from the bottom, so the word runs backwards

parts.note: taken as written, then read upwards

explanation.surface: Rod is single and not a snob.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rod' looks like a man's name; it is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: A baton is a short rod or stick, carried by a conductor or relay runner.

clue.text: Antelope seen in country, not Iran

indicators.note: not means without, so the letters for the other country are taken away

parts.note: a country
IR is the international code for Iran

explanation.surface: An antelope is spotted in one country but not Iran.
explanation.definitionFit: The eland is a large African antelope with spiral horns.

clue.text: Fake American policeman in New York

parts.note: a sham is a fake
US, the United States

explanation.surface: An impostor posing as a New York cop.
explanation.definitionFit: Shamus is American slang for a police officer or private detective.

clue.text: Sane public right to replace leader

indicators.note: the opening letter is swapped out and the new letter put in its place

parts.note: national means belonging to the public as a whole
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: A sensible public demands the right to replace its leader.
explanation.definitionFit: Rational means reasonable and of sound mind, i.e. sane.

clue.text: Small sweet potato

parts.note: S is the abbreviation for small
pud is short for pudding, a British word for dessert

explanation.surface: A little sweet potato.
explanation.walkthrough: 'sweet potato' reads as the vegetable; split it, and sweet is the dessert.
explanation.definitionFit: Spud is an informal word for a potato.

clue.text: Talks online after repellent creature given protective coat

indicators.note: to repel is to drive back, so this word is turned backwards

parts.note: an animal is a creature
TED Talks are lectures shared online

explanation.surface: Online chat about a nasty creature, plus some protective covering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'repellent' suggests disgusting; here it means driven back, so the creature reads backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: Laminated means covered with a thin protective layer, such as plastic film.
